d: Install Nostr Vault on an iPhone or iPad, create a Nostr account or bring the one you have, and find your way around.
h: Install · Pick a way in · Create an account · Bring the account you have · Who told you about Nostr Vault? · Find your way around · Next
x: Nostr Vault runs your own Nostr relay on your phone. Your posts, messages and media are kept on the phone, and copies go out to public relays so people can see them. Install Nostr Vault needs iOS 17 or later, on an iPhone or an iPad. Join the beta on TestFlight , install it, and open it. The first screen on iPhone Pick a way in The first screen has two buttons. What's inside? under them lists what the app does. Create an account if you're new to Nostr. You get a new key, a password for it and a profile. I already use Nostr if you have an account from another Nostr app. You bring that account, and your old notes come home to your phone. Create an account Welcome to Nostr. A short explanation of Nostr and your vault. Tap Create My Account . Your Keys. Two keys replace a username and password. The public key is your name on Nostr; share it freely. The secret key is your password; anyone who has it can post as you. Tap Copy next to the secret key and save it in your password manager. Nobody can recover it for you. Tick I saved my secret key , then Continue . Protect Your Key. Choose a password of at least 8 characters. This password locks the secret key you just saved. It stays on this device only and is never sent to us or any server. We cannot recover or reset it. If you forget it, the secret key you saved is your only way back in. Write it down and keep it with your secret key. Your Profile. Add a photo and a name, or tap Skip for Now . You can change both later. Your posts will be shared through these servers. The relays your posts go out to. Tap Continue to keep them, or Change to pick others. You can change them any time in Settings → Relays. Who told you about Nostr Vault? See below . Welcome to Nostr! Your account is made and your relay is running. Tap Start Exploring . Fill your feed. Nostr starts empty: no algorithm picks for you. Tap Let's fill it , pick a few topics, and follow people whose posts you like. Five follows build your web of trust, which fills your feed and filters out spam. Not now skips it. Your Keys (secret key hidden here) Protect Your Key Your Profile Fill your feed You're done when your Following feed shows posts from the people you followed. Bring the account you have Tap I already use Nostr . The screen asks Who are you on Nostr? Paste one of these into the box, or tap the QR icon ( Scan a QR code ) to scan one. The app tells you what you'll be able to do: You paste The app shows What you get Your npub, or name@domain Read-only (for name@domain, <name> · read-only ) Your feed, notes and follows. Add your secret key later in Settings to post. Your nsec (secret key) You can post Post, reply, DM and zap. You choose a password, and the key is saved encrypted on this phone. It's never sent anywhere. An ncryptsec (a key locked with a password) Encrypted key · you can post Enter the password you locked it with. A bunker:// link from a signer app Signer link · you can post Your signer app approves each post. Your key never touches Nostr Vault. To use a signer app instead, tap Use a signer app , then Sign in with Clave . See Signers . Do you have a Vault backup? If you have a backup .zip from Nostr Vault, tap Yes, restore my backup and pick it: your notes come back at once and the relay import is skipped. Otherwise tap No, import from my relays . Checking your relays. The app looks for your notes on the import relays, and also on the write relays you published yourself (marked yours ; read for this import only, never saved). When it's done the title says Ready to import . Change import relays lets you turn relays off or add one. Tap Start import . Bringing your notes home. A few cards explain what's happening while your notes are copied to your phone. A long history takes a while. Wait, or tap Keep it running in the background and start using the app; the import carries on. Who are you on Nostr?, with an npub pasted Checking your relays Pasting a secret key into any app is a risk. A signer keeps the key out

d: Install Nostr Vault on a Mac, set it up from the menu bar, and keep your relay running while the app is open.
h: Install · Pick a way in · Create an account · Bring the account you have · Who told you about Nostr Vault? · Just look around · Find your way around · Next
x: On a Mac, Nostr Vault lives in the menu bar and runs your own Nostr relay while it's open. Leave it running and your Mac becomes the always-on home for your notes and media. Install Nostr Vault needs macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later. Download it from the latest release on GitHub (the NostrVault-macOS-….zip file), unzip it, and drag Nostr Vault into Applications. The first time it opens, a Welcome to Nostr Vault window says Nostr Vault lives in your menu bar . Click Get Started . Setup opens next. The first window after install Pick a way in Create an account if you're new to Nostr. I already use Nostr to bring your account, your notes and your media. Just look around to read with your public key only. The three ways in on Mac Create an account The same steps as on the iPhone: Create My Account , save your secret key on Your Keys and tick I saved my secret key , choose a password on Protect Your Key , then a photo and name on Your Profile (or Skip for Now ), the relays your posts go to on Your posts will be shared through these servers , who told you , and Start Exploring . The details are on Get started on iPhone . About the password on Protect Your Key : This password locks the secret key you just saved. It stays on this device only and is never sent to us or any server. We cannot recover or reset it. If you forget it, the secret key you saved is your only way back in. Bring the account you have Enter Your Keys. Pick how you sign: Private Key : paste your nsec and choose a password. The key is encrypted on this Mac. Remote Signer : Connect with Clave on your iPhone shows a code to scan with Clave. Or paste a bunker link from any signer app. Your key stays in the signer. No account yet? New to Nostr? Generate Keys makes one here. A key made this way skips the servers step and the profile, so set your relays later in Settings → Relays. Your Vault. Your vault runs on this Mac either way. A Relay Domain (optional) makes it reachable from your other devices. Leave it blank for local only, or tap Skip — configure later . Do you have a Vault backup? Yes, restore my backup restores a Nostr Vault backup .zip and skips the relay import. No, import from my relays goes on to the import. Bring Your Notes Home. From Network copies your notes from public relays to this Mac, and also reads the write relays you published yourself (it says Also reading from your servers ); From Backup restores a Nostr Vault backup. Tap Import Notes , or Skip — I'll start fresh . Mirror Your Media. Copies your photos and videos from a media server, or from a backup, to this Mac. Tap Sync Media or Skip Media . Lightning (NWC). Paste a Nostr Wallet Connect link to send zaps, or Skip — set up later . You're All Set. Click Launch Nostr Vault . Enter Your Keys Your Vault Bring Your Notes Home You're All Set Who told you about Nostr Vault? Setup with a key you can post with asks who told you about Nostr Vault, just before the last screen. Paste their profile link or npub, check their profile card and follow them, then pick from up to 10 people they follow (all ticked to start). Skip, nobody told me leaves it out. On a Mac a profile link can't fill this in for you, so paste it. Details on Get started on iPhone . Just look around Enter Your Public Key (your npub or name@domain), answer Do you have a Vault backup? , import your notes if you like, and Ready to Browse opens the app. Re-run setup later to post, DM and zap. Find your way around Click the Nostr Vault icon in the menu bar. The panel shows your relay's status, your notes and your media. Open Full App opens the full window, with the feed. The gear at the bottom ( Settings (⌘,) ) opens Settings. Your relay runs while Nostr Vault is open. The power button next to it ( Quit Nostr Vault ) stops it. To keep it running, open Settings → Startup and turn on Launch at Login and Start Vault Automatically . The menu bar panel Settings, Startup Next The mesh : make your Mac the home vault for your phones. Your keys and accounts

t: Use Nostr Vault in a browser
d: Open the Nostr Vault web app at nostrvault.app/vault/, create an account or sign in with a browser extension, a bunker link or read-only, and know what the web app keeps in your browser.
h: New to Nostr · Sign in · The first sign-in · Opening a shared post · Find your way around · Browsers · Your data in this browser · Next
x: The web app is Nostr Vault in a browser tab, with nothing to install. Open nostrvault.app/vault/ in any up-to-date browser, on a computer or a phone. Like the apps, it runs your own relay, here inside the browser. Your notes and messages are kept in this browser's storage. New to Nostr Click Create an account , then Create My Account . The web app makes your keys in this browser and shows both. Save the secret key somewhere safe, tick I saved my secret key , and choose a password of at least 8 characters, typed twice. Add a name and photo if you like, or Skip for Now . Pick some people to follow. The next screen, Your posts will be shared through these servers , lists the relays your posts go out to: Continue keeps them, Change picks others. Then click Start Exploring . The secret key stays in this browser, locked with your password; it is never sent anywhere. To see it again, open Settings → Your Secret Key and type your password. Signing out, or the browser clearing this site's data, deletes it from this browser, and nobody can recover it for you. The web app can't sign in with a secret key, so to use the account again, add the copy you saved to a Nostr browser extension and click I already use Nostr , or import it in the Nostr Vault app. Sign in Already use Nostr? Click I already use Nostr . The web app never asks for the secret key of an account you already have. Sign in with something that holds the key for you: A browser extension. Click Sign in with extension and approve in the extension. If this browser has no Nostr extension, the button shows which one to install instead: Sidecar for Chrome, Brave, Edge and Firefox; Nostash on a Mac; and on iPhone and iPad, Safari with Nostr Build Shack or Nostash . Android browsers can't add one yet, so use a bunker link from Amber. A remote signer. Paste a bunker:// link (or your name@domain) from your signer app into Bunker link (NIP-46) , click Connect bunker , and approve the connection in your signer. See Signers . Read-only. Type your npub or name@domain and click Sign in read-only , or type a plain name and click Find me to pick yourself from the results. You can read your feed but not post. The sign-in screen in a desktop browser Accounts you've used in this browser are listed at the top next time, so one click signs you back in. To keep several accounts signed in, use Settings → Accounts & Keys → Add Account . Just want to look? Just look around on the first screen finds anyone on Nostr by name, npub or NIP-05, without an account. The first sign-in The first time an account signs in here, Getting your vault ready starts your relay in the browser, finds your account and fetches your notes and the notes of people you follow. Wait, or click Open now, finish in the background . To fetch your older posts later, open Settings → Import Notes , pick a start date and click Import from my relays . Opening a shared post A post shared from Nostr Vault opens in the web app, and anyone can read it without signing in. The top says Viewing as a guest . Click Sign in there to reply, like or zap. A guest's browser keeps nothing once the tab is closed. Find your way around The same places as the phone apps: Feed , Search , Profile , WoT and Vault . On a phone they're a tab bar at the bottom; in a wide window they're a sidebar, and a post opens next to the list. Settings is the gear on your profile. Your relays are in Settings → Relays . Changes are kept only when you click Save and publish , which publishes your relay list for other apps; your phone uses the same list. Browsers The web app runs in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari. On iPhone and iPad it needs iOS 16.4 or later, and on a Mac Safari 16.4 or later; keep other browsers up to date. An older browser shows a blank page. It needs WebAssembly and site storage (IndexedDB). Lockdown Mode on iPhone, iPad or Mac turns WebAssembly off, so the app says Your relay didn't start . Turn Lockdown Mode off for nostrvault.app in its web browsing set

d: What your Nostr keys are, where Nostr Vault keeps them, and how to add accounts, switch between them, back up your secret key and remove a key.
h: Two keys · Where to find them · Add another account · Switch accounts · Back up your secret key · Change how an account signs · Remove a key or an account · Your relay list · Next
x: A Nostr account is a pair of keys. Nostr Vault keeps them on your device, or leaves the secret one with a signer app, and never on a server. Two keys Public key (starts with npub ): your name on Nostr. Share it freely. With only this, an app can show your feed but can't post as you. Secret key (starts with nsec ): your password to Nostr. Anyone who has it can post as you, forever. Nobody can reset it or recover it for you, not even us. Nostr Vault can sign for you in two ways: A local key. Your secret key, locked with a password you choose (at least 8 characters), and kept on this device only. A key locked this way starts with ncryptsec . This password locks your secret key. It stays on this device only and is never sent to us or any server. We cannot recover or reset it. If you forget it, your saved secret key is your only way back in. A signer. A separate app holds your secret key and approves each post. Nostr Vault never sees the key. See Signers . Where to find them Device Open iPhone, iPad, Android Profile tab → gear → Accounts & Keys Mac Menu bar icon → gear → Accounts & Keys Web Settings → Accounts & Keys Each account shows how it signs: Local Key , Remote Signer , Amber (Android), or No signing key (read-only). The first account you set up is the Owner : it's the one your vault belongs to. Tap an account to manage it. On iPhone, iPad and Mac it opens its own page; on Android its row opens in place. Accounts & Keys on iPhone An account on iPhone An account on Android Add another account In Accounts & Keys , tap Add Account . Paste the account's key. iPhone, iPad and Mac take its npub. Then open the new account and tap Import Private Key or Connect Remote Signer to post with it. Android takes an npub, an nsec or an ncryptsec, or Connect Remote Signer (NIP-46) . Web signs in with the account's own extension or bunker. The account you're using stays signed in. Accounts & Keys on Mac Switch accounts iPhone: hold your picture in the middle of the tab bar and pick an account. It only opens when you have more than one. Mac: the account button in the menu bar panel. Everywhere: open the account in Accounts & Keys and tap Switch to This Account . A post is always sent from the account that was active when you tapped Post. Back up your secret key Do this once, right after you make an account, and keep the key in a password manager. Open the account in Accounts & Keys . Tap Reveal Key (Android: Reveal Private Key ). The app checks it's you with Face ID, Touch ID or your device passcode, then asks for the key's password. Copy the key into your password manager. Don't paste it into a chat, a note or a screenshot. Reveal Private Key, still locked With a signer, there's no key to reveal here. Back it up in the signer app. Change how an account signs Import Private Key adds a local key to an account that only had a public key or a signer. Tick Encrypt with Password to lock it. Connect Remote Signer adds a signer. It must hold this account's key; a signer for another account is refused. With both, Sign With (Android: Signing ) picks which one signs. Remove a key or an account Remove Local Key deletes the secret key from this device. If it's your only copy, it's gone for good. Disconnect Remote Signer drops the signer's connection. Reconnecting needs a fresh bunker link. Remove Account takes the account, and any key or signer for it, off this device. Nothing on the relays changes, but you need the key again to sign back in. Your relay list Your relay list (NIP-65) tells other Nostr apps which relays you read from and write to, so they can find your posts and reach you. There is no separate publish button any more: the list is published only when you tap Save in Settings → Relays (on the web, Save and publish ). Your DM inbox list is published by the same Save. Next Signers : Amber, Clave, bunker links and browser extensions.

d: Keep your Nostr secret key out of Nostr Vault with a signer: Amber on Android, Clave on iPhone, a bunker link from any signer app, or a browser extension on the web.
h: Which signer, where · Sign in with a signer during setup · Add a signer to an account you already have · On the web · Good to know
x: A signer is a separate app that holds your secret key. When Nostr Vault wants to post, like or send a message as you, it asks the signer, and the signer approves. Your key never enters Nostr Vault, so a problem in Nostr Vault can't leak it. Which signer, where Device Signers How it connects Android Amber, or any signer app on the phone Use Amber , or Use a signer app → Sign in with a signer app iPhone and iPad Clave Use a signer app → Sign in with Clave Mac Clave on your iPhone Connect with Clave on your iPhone shows a code to scan Web A Nostr browser extension. On iPhone and iPad: Nostr Build Shack or Nostash in Safari Sign in with extension Everywhere Any signer that gives a bunker link (NIP-46), such as nsec.app or your own bunker Paste or scan the bunker:// link Sign in with a signer during setup Choose I already use Nostr . On iPhone and Android, the next screen has Use a signer app under the box (and Use Amber on Android when Amber is installed). On a Mac, choose Remote Signer . The signer opens, or a code shows on screen to scan with a signer on another device. Approve the connection in the signer, then come back to Nostr Vault. If the signer didn't open, tap Open Clave again (Android: Open signer again ), or Copy link and open it yourself. Or paste a bunker:// link from any signer app into the same box. Remote Signer on Mac: Connect with Clave on your iPhone Add a signer to an account you already have Open Settings → Accounts & Keys and tap the account. Tap Connect Remote Signer . Paste the bunker link into Bunker URI , or scan its QR code. On iPhone you can Sign in with Clave here too. Approve the connection in your signer app. Connect a signer on iPhone Connect Remote Signer on Android The signer has to hold this account's key. A signer for a different account is refused. On the web An account you already have signs on the web with a signer: a browser extension, or a bunker link in Bunker link (NIP-46) and Connect bunker . It never asks for that account's secret key. (An account made with Create an account on the web keeps its key in that browser, locked with your password: see Use Nostr Vault in a browser .) A bunker's connection to the browser is stored encrypted, and removing the account or signing out asks the bunker to drop it. Good to know Posts, likes and messages are signed by the signer, which may ask you to approve each one. If nothing happens, open the signer and check for a pending request. To stop using a signer, open the account and tap Disconnect Remote Signer . Revoke the connection in the signer app too. Back up your secret key in the signer app. Nostr Vault can't show it to you, because it never has it.

d: How the Nostr Vault wallet works: connect a Lightning wallet with a Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) link, turn on zap buttons, disconnect, and the on-chain Bitcoin address under Advanced.
h: What the wallet is · Connect a wallet · Turning on zap buttons · Saving the wallet to your Nostr account · Disconnecting · Bitcoin On-Chain · The Wallet Connect tutorial
x: The basics What the wallet is A zap is a small bitcoin tip sent over Lightning (bitcoin's fast payment network) to the person who posted. Amounts are in sats , the smallest unit of bitcoin. Nostr Vault never holds that money. Your sats stay in a Lightning wallet you run somewhere else, such as Alby Hub, Coinos, Primal or Zeus. Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) is a standard way for an app to ask that wallet to pay. Your wallet gives you a link that starts with nostr+walletconnect:// , and you paste it into Nostr Vault. Treat the link like cash. Anyone who has it can spend from that wallet. If your wallet lets you, make a connection with a spending limit just for Nostr Vault. Step by step Connect a wallet In your wallet app, find Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) and copy the connection link. In Nostr Vault, open Settings → Account → Wallet . Paste the link into the Wallet Connect box (on Android it's called Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) ). On the web, tap Connect a wallet , paste the link, then tap Connect wallet . The app pastes the link only. There is no QR scanner for it. Once a wallet is connected you'll see its Balance and can set your Default Zap (on Android, Default Zap Amount (sats) ), the amount one tap sends. On the web, Default zap is there even before you connect. On every device, including the web, you can also start from your own profile. Tap the bolt (labelled Lightning in the apps, Wallet on the web). With no wallet yet, it shows No Wallet Connected and a Connect a wallet button that takes you to the same place. On Android the wallet is on the Settings tab of that screen. Once connected, that screen shows your balance and lets you receive with an invoice, pay an invoice, lightning address or LNURL, and see your history if your wallet shares it. Opt in Turning on zap buttons Zap buttons on posts are a choice you make under Settings → Appearance → Post buttons . Add ⚡️ in the Add ⚡️ field to show a zap button, and remove it to hide the button. Zapping someone from their profile is always available. iPhone, iPad and Mac: the zap button is off until you add ⚡️. It then shows on posts, live streams and locked articles. Android: ⚡️ is there by default, so posts show a zap button until you remove it. Web: notes show a zap button. A tap sends your default zap, and holding it lets you pick another amount. Turn off Zap button ⚡️ under Settings → Post buttons to hide it. Each zap goes straight from your wallet to the author. Nostr Vault takes no cut. Phones and Mac Saving the wallet to your Nostr account On iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android, the Wallet page can switch on Save wallet to my Nostr account . The link is then stored encrypted to your key on your relays, so Nostr Vault on your other devices (or the Wisp app) can pick it up with Use saved wallet . Anyone who has your Nostr key can read it and spend from the wallet. Remove from my account takes it off again. Stop using it Disconnecting iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android: delete the link from the Wallet Connect box. If you saved it to your account, also tap Remove from my account . Web: tap Disconnect wallet , then Disconnect . The web app keeps the link only in that browser, and deletes it when you sign out. To be sure the app can't spend any more, also revoke the connection in your wallet app. Advanced Bitcoin On-Chain Separate from Lightning, the apps can make a regular bitcoin address from your Nostr key. It lives under Settings → Advanced → Bitcoin On-Chain on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android. It isn't in the web app. Turn on Bitcoin Address to see the address and a QR code, and use Copy Address to share it. Sweep Wallet sends everything at that address to another address you choose. This one is different. Bitcoin sent to this address is controlled by your Nostr key, so anyone with your key can spend it. Before a sweep, the app warns you not to send to a hardware wallet or an exchange: that would tie your npub to that walle

d: Nostr Vault feeds: Following, Discover, Global, Popular, Media and the rest; Edit Feeds; the Web of Trust shield; languages; reposts, replies and auto-load; and how a new account fills its feed.
h: The feeds · Edit Feeds · Web of Trust or Everyone · The buttons at the top · New posts · Feed & Display · Spam and blocking · Filling an empty feed · On each device
x: The feeds Tap the feed name at the top left of the Feed tab to switch. On iPhone you can also hold the Feed tab and slide up. Following : people you follow. It's always on. Discover : the people your follows follow. Global : everyone in your web of trust , without replies. Hashtags : the hashtags you follow. Popular : what's getting the most replies, reposts, likes and zaps. Media : photos and videos. diVines : short looping videos. Articles : long-form posts. An edited article shows once. Recipes : recipes posted for zap.cooking. Marketplace : things for sale. Live : live streams, loaded fresh each time. Polls : polls you can vote in. Music : tracks from Wavlake. Pick yours Edit Feeds Open the feed menu and tap Edit Feeds at the bottom. Tap a feed to show or hide it. Drag a feed to move it. On Android, drag the handle. Tap Reset to Default to start over. Following can't be hidden. If you hide the feed you're on, you go back to Following. Spam stays out Web of Trust or Everyone Global, Hashtags, and the Global side of Media, Articles, diVines, Recipes, Live, Marketplace and Polls show only people in your web of trust: people you follow and the people they follow. A shield at the top right says Web of Trust . Tap it to switch to Everyone . You'll get a Sensitive Content Warning first, because Everyone is unfiltered and you should expect spam. It starts on Web of Trust. Everyone stays locked until you follow at least 5 people. Until then the shield shows a lock, and tapping it explains why: Everyone is locked , how many of the 5 you follow, and how many more to go, for example "Follow 3 more people to unlock Everyone". Follow a few people and the switch opens. If you had already turned Everyone on, it stays on. If your web isn't built yet, Global and Media stay empty. Hashtags and Live show everyone instead, so you can find your first people. Live still leaves out adult streams. Tune a feed The buttons at the top Each feed shows the buttons that make sense for it. Reposts and Auto-load on Following, Discover and Global, and Replies on Following and Discover. Global never shows replies. d: How Nostr Vault notifications work without APNs or FCM push on iPhone, Android, Mac and the web app: what wakes the app, when alerts arrive while it is open, in the background or closed, what to allow, and the limits.
h: Why there is no push · iPhone: when iOS lets it run · Android: your vault keeps running · Mac: always on while it's running · Web: only while a tab is open
x: Why there is no push Most apps get their alerts from a company server, which hands them to Apple (APNs) or Google (FCM) to send to your phone. That server sees who wrote to you and when. Nostr Vault has no such server. The relay inside the app collects what tags you, and the app makes the notification itself on your device. So an alert can only come while that relay is running. How often it can run is different on each device. On every device: Only people in your web of trust set off an alert. New followers from outside it are counted ("3 new followers") instead of named. You choose the kinds under Settings → Notifications ( more ). Likes and reposts are off until you turn them on. While the app is open, new things show as a pill at the top, not as a system alert. With more than one account, each alert shows which account it's for, and each account's alerts are grouped together. In the account switcher, each other account shows how many new things it has. Something older than 24 hours never sets off an alert. When the vault catches up after being away, the first five items alert and the rest fold into one summary. iPhone and iPad iPhone: when iOS lets it run What wakes it: iOS's Background App Refresh. The app asks to be woken every 15 minutes at the earliest. iOS decides when that actually happens, based on how often you use the app, your battery and your connection. There is also a longer check that iOS only runs while the phone is charging and online. Open: things arrive right away and show as a pill at the top. They are also listed in Notification Center. In the background: the app keeps going for about 30 seconds after you leave it, then iOS pauses it. After that, alerts come only when iOS wakes the app. That can be minutes later or much longer. Swiped away: this stops your vault. iOS may not wake an app you swiped away until you open it again, so alerts wait until then. With a Mac: if your Mac is your vault, each wake asks it for what came in while the phone was asleep. The Mac is always listening, so less is missed. What to allow: notifications (the app asks during setup), and iOS Settings → General → Background App Refresh on for Nostr Vault. The app doesn't check that second one for you. Low Power Mode pauses Background App Refresh. The honest limit: an iPhone without a home vault is not instant. If you need alerts right away, keep a home vault running or open the app. Android Android: your vault keeps running What wakes it: nothing has to. Your vault runs as a service you can see: the Your Vault notification, which says Vault running and has a Stop Vault button. It listens to your relays all the time and checks for anything it missed every 15 minutes. Open: new things show as a pill. Pills you didn't look at are filed quietly under Missed while open . In the background or swiped away: alerts come right away, because the vault keeps running. After a restart or an app update: the vault starts again by itself, as long as Start Vault Automatically is on (it is unless you turned it off, under Settings → Your Vault ). Force stopped or Stop Vault: no alerts until you open the app again. Using another app's relay (such as Citrine) instead of the built-in one: Nostr Vault makes no alerts. What to allow: notifications. On Android 13 and newer, setup asks with Enable Notifications , and turning on Settings → Notifications asks again if you said no. The honest limit: some phones' battery savers close background apps anyway, and the app doesn't ask to be left alone. If alerts stop, set Nostr Vault's battery use to Unrestricted in Android's settings. If the vault keeps failing, it stops restarting itself after four tries in six hours; opening the app starts it again. Mac Mac: always on while it's running What wakes it: nothing has to. Nostr Vault lives in the menu bar, with no Dock icon, and your vault keeps running when you close its window. It listens to your relays all the time. Running: alerts come right away, as normal Mac no

d: Nostr Vault's web of trust: the WoT tab globe, layers (Following, Vouched, Further out), Find someone, trust paths, My Web, Rebuild your web, and the Who Can Reach You settings.
h: What it is · The globe · Trust paths and their web · My Web and rebuilding · What your web decides · Who Can Reach You · On each device
x: What it is Nostr has no central moderator. Instead, Nostr Vault trusts who you trust. Your web has three rings: Following : the people you follow. Vouched : people that 10 or more of your follows follow. Further out : people your follows follow, but fewer than 10 of them. Your vault rebuilds the web on its own, once a day unless you change Refresh Trust List. If you follow very few people, it borrows from your follows' follows so a new account isn't empty. The WoT tab The globe Open the WoT tab. You're in the middle. Your follows sit on the first ring, Vouched people on the next, and everyone else is a faint outer shell. Each person always sits in the same spot, because their place comes from their key. Layers. The menu at the top left picks Everyone , Following , Vouched or Further out , each with a count. Vouched shows up once your vault has counted your web. Filters. Talk with you keeps people you've replied to, reposted, liked or zapped, or who did that to you. Follow you back keeps follows who follow you too. Find someone. Tap the magnifier and type a name. Your follows come first, then your web, then everyone else. Why someone is here Trust paths and their web Tap a face to open their card. The line under their name says how they reach you, for example "You follow them · 1 hop" or "Followed by Ann, Bo + more you follow · 2 hops". If no one you follow follows them, it says "Not in your web". From the card you can follow or unfollow, open their Profile , or tap See their web to put them in the middle and see the globe from their side. A globe opened from a profile or a post has Open in WoT instead, which takes you to the WoT tab. A post's Event Info shows the same trust path for its author. The numbers My Web and rebuilding Tap My Web for the whole picture: how many people are in your web, how many you follow, how many are Vouched, who talks with you and who follows you back. Under Upkeep it says when the web was last rebuilt. Just followed a lot of people? Tap Rebuild your web (in My Web, or at the bottom of the layer menu). The globe shows each step: reading your follow list, reading your follows' lists, counting. A full rebuild can take a few minutes. If it fails or the vault isn't running, the globe keeps your last saved web. Where it's used What your web decides Who can reach your vault. Only people in your web can post to your vault's inbox. Strangers can still reply to or quote your own posts. Notifications. Replies, likes, reposts and mentions notify you only from people in your web. Zaps and follows always come through. A message alerts if it's from your web or someone you've written to; others wait under Requests. A new follower outside your web is folded into "N new followers". Feeds. Global, Media and the other discovery feeds show only your web unless you switch them to Everyone. Everyone unlocks once you follow 5 people. See Feeds . Search. Your follows and your web rank above everyone else. Mesh photos. Photos load over the mesh only from people you follow, not from your wider web. Settings Who Can Reach You On iPhone and Android, open Settings → Your Vault → Who Can Reach You . Follow Distance sets how far out your web reaches (3, your whole web, to start), Minimum Followers how many of your follows must vouch for someone further out, and Refresh Trust List how often it's rebuilt. Details on Who Can Reach You . On each device iPhone, iPad and Android have everything on this page. The web app has a WoT tab with the Globe , the Everyone, Following, Vouched and Further out layers, Find someone , Follow you back , trust cards with See their web , and My Web with Rebuild your web . It builds your web in the browser from follow lists, so it has no Talk with you filter and no trust settings. Replay it in the app: Settings → Help → Tutorials → Your Web of Trust .

d: How Nostr Vault's mesh works: your phone or Mac serves your own photos over the mesh, with no public IP, domain or cloud. My Devices, Home vault mode, share pages and privacy.
h: What the mesh is · Your phone or Mac as your photo server · My Devices · Home vault mode · Share pages · Privacy · What works today
x: The basics What the mesh is Most phones and home computers can't be reached from the internet. They sit behind a home router, move between Wi-Fi and cell, and have no fixed address. That's why your photos normally live on someone else's server. The mesh (built on FIPS) is a network where you reach a device by its Nostr key (an npub) instead of an IP address. It works across home routers and mobile networks, and the connection between two devices is encrypted end to end. Nostr Vault uses it to let your devices reach each other, and to let other people fetch your photos from you. Photos stay trustworthy no matter who hands them over. On Nostr, a photo is named by its fingerprint (a hash). Whoever sends it, the app checks the fingerprint, and if it matches, it's the photo. If it doesn't, the photo is thrown away and loaded the normal way. Your own server Your phone or Mac as your photo server Your Nostr profile already keeps a list of where your media lives. Nostr Vault adds one more entry to that list: your home vault (your Mac or a spare phone), written as its mesh address. Your everyday phone isn't listed. It goes after your normal media servers, so apps that don't know about the mesh carry on as before. An app that does know about it can ask your device for a photo directly, by its fingerprint, the same way it would ask any media server. Your photos still go to your normal servers too. Your device is one more place they can come from, and the one you own. On a Mac , the Nostr Vault app serves while it's open. Leave it running and your Mac is an always-on photo server. On a phone , it serves while the app is open, or full-time in Home vault mode on a spare phone. Step by step: your Mac as your photo server , home vault . To turn it on, open Settings → Mesh and switch on Mesh . Serving is off until you turn it on. Your devices, together My Devices My Devices is the list of your own phones, Macs, home vault and browser vault that reach each other over the mesh. Devices on this list sync with each other in full: your notes, your photos and your history. On each device, open Settings → Mesh , turn on Mesh , and in This Device tap Copy . That's the device's mesh address. On your other devices, go to My Devices → Add a device by address , paste it, and pick what it is: Home vault · full history , Home vault · new posts , Phone or Browser vault . Do it in both directions: add each phone on the Mac, and the Mac on each phone. A device on the list shows a dot when it's in reach. To check that everything arrived, use Mesh → Sync → Check sync on a phone. An always-on vault Home vault mode Home vault mode turns a phone into a small always-on vault. Put an old phone on a charger at home, turn Home vault mode on under Share With Others , and it keeps serving. On iPhone it keeps the screen on, pauses when you leave the app and turns on again when you come back. On Android it keeps serving in the background while the vault runs. Your own devices in My Devices reach it in full. Everyone else can only read the photos in your posts, and only slowly: 1 MB/s shared between all of them, at most 256 MB each. On iPhone they get 1 GB a day in total, then wait until the next day. On Android, Pause after sets the total for one session (1 GB to start). They can't read your notes or change anything. Add it on your other phones as Home vault · new posts , and your new notes and photos go to the home vault over the mesh, which sends your notes on to your relays. Works in any browser Share pages When you share a post from Nostr Vault, the link opens that post in the Nostr Vault web app, in any normal browser. Anyone can read it as a guest, with no account and nothing to install, and sign in from there to reply or like. If a photo in that post or its replies can't be loaded from its usual server, the browser fetches it from that author's own device over the mesh.
