h: Set it up · Check that it arrived · Good to know
x: With your Mac on your phone's list as Home vault · full history , each new note and photo you post on the phone also goes to the Mac over the mesh. Your notes and history sync back from the Mac to the phone. The Mac becomes the second, always-on copy of your vault. Set it up Turn on the mesh on the Mac and on the phone, and add each to the other's My Devices . On the phone, pick Home vault · full history . Keep Nostr Vault open on the Mac. It syncs while it's open. Shortly after the phone's vault starts, it copies your full history from the Mac on its own. After that, new posts and mentions keep syncing by themselves. Check that it arrived On iPhone and Android, open Settings → Mesh and, under Sync , tap Check home vault sync . It's also under Settings → Home vault sync . It ends with what was copied and how many are missing (Done · nothing missing on iPhone, Everything copied · 0 missing on Android), or says why it stopped. Sync, with Check home vault sync Copying your full history from the Mac… : the first copy is still running. Leave the app open. Copy was interrupted : the app closed during the copy. It picks up again the next time the relay starts. If you also have a home vault , Send now under Sync sends what's waiting for it. Good to know Nothing goes through a server of ours. The phone and the Mac talk over the mesh, end to end encrypted. When the Mac is closed or out of reach, new posts still go to your public relays as usual. The Mac catches up when it's back. Posting a photo still needs a public media server. The Mac gets a copy as well.

d: Your home vault is the always-on one: a Mac, Linux box, Pi, box or spare phone that stays on. What each kind does, and how to turn a spare phone into one with Home vault mode.
h: What each kind does · 1. Turn on Home vault mode on the spare phone · 2. Add it to My Devices · Photos go to
x: Your home vault is the vault that stays on. It can be a Mac, a Linux box or Raspberry Pi, a box, or an old phone on a charger. Your other devices reach it over the mesh, so your notes and media have a home even when your phone is off. What each kind does Home vault · full history (a Mac today; Linux and Pi later): keeps all your history and syncs both ways with your phones. Set it up with Home vault sync . Home vault · new posts (a spare phone or a box): keeps your new posts and media, and passes your notes on to your relays. It doesn't hold your older history. This page shows how to set one up on a spare phone. 1. Turn on Home vault mode on the spare phone Install Nostr Vault on the spare phone and sign in with the same account. On iPhone, add your main phone under My Devices first (step 2). Home vault mode won't start with an empty list. Open Settings → Mesh , switch on Mesh , and under Share With Others switch on Home vault mode . Leave it on a charger. On iPhone, Home vault mode keeps the screen on, pauses when you leave the app and turns on again when you come back. On Android it keeps serving in the background while your vault runs, and after a restart. Your devices in My Devices reach the home vault in full. Anyone else on the mesh can read only the photos in your posts, and slowly: 1 MB/s for all of them together, at most 256 MB each. On iPhone they get 1 GB a day in total, then wait until the next day. They can't read your notes or change anything. On Android, Pause after (250 MB, 1 GB or 5 GB, 1 GB to start) sets how much the mesh may download in one session. When it's reached, Home vault mode turns off until you turn it on again. Share With Others on iPhone Share With Others on Android, with Pause after 2. Add it to My Devices On the spare phone, under This Device , copy its mesh address (or show its QR code). On your main phone, open Settings → Mesh → Add a device by address , paste or scan it, and pick Home vault · new posts . A home vault your account already lists shows under Address as In your media servers (on Android, In Your Media Servers ). Tap it to use its address. Add the main phone to the spare phone's My Devices too. From then on, your new notes and media also go to the home vault over the mesh, and it sends your notes on to your relays. They stay on your main phone too. Anything that can't reach it waits on the main phone and goes when the app is open and the home vault is in reach. Send now under Sync sends it straight away. What's public. A home vault's mesh address is listed in your media server list, in public, so other apps can fetch your photos from it. Direct-message attachments are never sent there. If your key is in a remote signer, media only goes to the home vault when you tap Send now . Photos go to Under Share With Others, Photos go to ( Media servers , Home vault or Both ) saves where you want photos to go, but it doesn't change anything yet: posting a photo still needs a public media server.

t: Your Mac as your photo server
d: Let Nostr Vault on your Mac serve your photos over the mesh, listed in your media servers, with no public IP, domain or port forwarding.
h: Turn it on · Who gets what · Privacy
x: Your Nostr profile keeps a list of where your media lives. Nostr Vault on your Mac can add itself to that list, written as its mesh address. Apps that can use the mesh then load your photos straight from your Mac. Apps that can't skip it and use your other media servers, as before. Turn it on On the Mac, open Settings → Mesh and switch on Mesh . The mesh engine runs inside the Mac app; there's nothing else to install. Add a phone under My Devices . The mesh starts once at least one of your devices is on that list, and the Mac then lists its mesh address in your media servers by itself. Keep Nostr Vault open. In Settings → Startup , turn on Launch at Login and Start Vault Automatically so it's always there. Share With Others on Mac: List in my media servers Who gets what Your own devices in My Devices reach the Mac's vault in full. Anyone else can only open photos and files by their link, at up to 1 MB/s. They can't read your notes or change anything. Your photos still go to your normal media servers too. The Mac is one more place they can come from, and the one you own. Privacy Your home IP isn't published. The list holds the Mac's mesh key, and the mesh finds it by key. Listing it does link your npub to the Mac's mesh key, in public. Removing it later doesn't erase older copies of your list that relays may still hold. List in my media servers (under Share With Others) and Address source (under Advanced) are only for an outside FIPS transport such as nostr-vpn. With My Nostr npub it lists your Nostr npub, not the Mac's mesh key. Leave them off otherwise. More on how photos are checked on the way: The mesh .

t: Remove a device, or a lost phone
d: Take a device off My Devices so it can no longer reach your vault, and what to do when a phone with Nostr Vault is lost or stolen.
h: Remove a device · A lost or stolen phone
x: Removing a device from My Devices stops it reaching this device's vault. Do it on every device that has it on its list. Remove a device Open Settings → Mesh and tap the device under My Devices . On the Mac, use the remove button on its row. Tap Remove from My Devices (on iPhone, confirm). On Android and with the Mac's minus button it goes at once. Repeat on each of your other devices. A device on Android, with Remove from My Devices What changes: It can no longer reach this device's vault, or learn its address. New notes and media stop going to it. A home vault also leaves your media server list. Anything it already has stays on it. Removing a device doesn't wipe it. A lost or stolen phone Remove it from My Devices on your Mac, your home vault and your other phones, as above. Signer: if the phone signed through a signer app, revoke its connection in the signer. Your key was never on the phone. Local key: if your secret key was on the phone, it's locked with your key password. Someone with the phone still needs that password. If you think they have it, treat the key as exposed: a Nostr key can't be changed, so make a new account and tell people to follow it. Set up the new phone : sign in with your key or signer ( iPhone , Android ), then add it to My Devices on your other devices. Your notes come back from your relays, your Mac or your home vault. Your public posts are on public relays and stay there. A lost phone loses only what nothing else holds a copy of, which is why a Mac or home vault is worth having.

t: Mesh settings: finder relays and middle server
d: What the finder relays and the middle server do in Nostr Vault's mesh settings, what they can see, and when to change them.
h: Finder Relays · Middle Server
x: Open Settings → Mesh → Advanced . Most people never need to change these. On iPhone, changes apply the next time the mesh starts. On Android they apply right away. Mesh, Advanced Finder Relays Your devices post where they are on these relays, so your other devices can find them. Like any relay, they see this device's IP address. Swipe to remove one on iPhone, or tap Remove on Android. At least one must stay. Middle Server The middle server links two devices that can't reach each other directly. It's how this phone reaches anyone outside My Devices: the photos of people you follow, a browser vault, and visitors to your home vault. They never get this phone's address, but the middle server does see it. Which follows' photos your app loads is up to you; who can see your photos isn't a setting. Public (fips1, fips2.iris.to) : the default on iPhone. On Android the default is None, so pick Public for follows' photos, a browser vault and home vault visitors. None : only devices on the same network can connect. Follows' photos load from their web addresses instead, a browser vault only connects on the same network, and a home vault takes no visitors. Reset to defaults puts both lists back.

d: The Nostr Vault browser vault at nostrvault.app/relay/: a browser tab that keeps your notes and serves them to your own devices over the mesh. Pairing, Start mesh, the screensaver, My Devices and limits.
h: What the browser vault is · Pair your iPhone with the page · What it keeps and serves · The screensaver · When the tab closes · In My Devices · Limits and privacy
x: The basics What the browser vault is The browser vault keeps your notes like any vault, but it runs inside a web page, at nostrvault.app/relay/ . It stores notes in the browser's own storage on that device and joins the mesh, so your own devices can reach it by its key. New to the mesh? Read The mesh first. The page keeps no Nostr key of yours. Your notes arrive already signed, and the page checks each signature. A good spot for it is an old phone or tablet on a charger. Set it up Pair your iPhone with the page On your iPhone, open Mesh and turn the mesh on. Under This Device , tap Copy . That's the phone's mesh address. On the device that will run the page, open nostrvault.app/relay/ . Paste the address into the box under the FIPS heading (one address per line). In the box below it, paste your Nostr account's npub: without it the page turns your notes away and keeps 0. Tap Save owners . The page reloads. Tap Start mesh . The status's first line shows the page's own mesh address . There's no Copy button, so select the address and copy it. On the iPhone, go to My Devices → Add a device by address , paste the page's address, and pick Browser vault . The phone then connects for the page. If it doesn't, open the page's entry in My Devices and tap Connect this phone . Copy this phone's mesh address is there too. A link of the form nostrvault.app/relay/#owner=npub1 also adds an owner. The npub in it is the phone's mesh address (from This Device ), not your Nostr account. The page asks you to confirm each address first, because an owner can write to the page and read everything on it. Only accept your own. What it does What it keeps and serves Your new notes. While the iPhone app is open, each new note you post also goes to the page. Send my latest notes sends your 20 most recent notes from the phone. The result line says how many the page kept. In this testing build, check that number: if it says 0 kept, the page did not take your notes. Checked notes only. The page checks each note's signature and turns away notes from authors it isn't set up for. Owners only, for notes. The page serves notes on the mesh only to the addresses saved as owners. Anyone else asking for notes is dropped without an answer. A public photo door. Like the apps, Start mesh also opens a public photo door on the mesh to anyone, and it answers only for photos that a public note names. Photos, read only. Under Show photo , you can paste a photo's fingerprint (sha256) or a .fips link and the page fetches it from a paired vault. It shows the photo only if the fingerprint matches. Photos aren't stored on the page. The page reaches your phone through the public mesh entry points (seeds). Once both ends are connected it tries a direct link. On the iPhone, leave the middle server under Advanced on its public setting. A browser vault has no same-network route, so with None it most likely can't reach your phone at all. Keep it awake The screensaver Start screensaver fills the screen with a black "relay running" view: a count, the uptime, whether the screen is kept awake (the wake lock), and whether the seed is up. Tap anywhere to leave it. After a reload, start it again. The count on this screen is the page's own test notes, not your notes. Report shows storage, uptime gaps and a signature self-test, if you want the details. When it stops When the tab closes The relay only runs while the page is open and the screen is on. Closed, locked or in the background, nothing reaches it. Notes the phone sends while the page is down are not queued. Tap Send my latest notes once it's back. Stored notes stay in the browser and are there when you reopen the page. Tap Start mesh again; it doesn't start by itself. Stop mesh takes the page off the mesh. The page's mesh key lives in the browser's site data. Clear that data and the page gets a new address, so pair it again. Your devices list In My Devices The page shows up in My Devices as a Browser vault , the role whose job reads "Gets

d: What your vault keeps on each device: your notes, mentions, messages and media. The Vault tab, starting and stopping it, Import Notes, and the Mac and web differences.
h: What your vault is · The Vault tab · Vault settings · Import your past notes · Phone, Mac and web
x: The basics What your vault is Most Nostr apps only read and write to other people's relays. Nostr Vault also runs one on your device. Your vault is a Nostr relay and media server of your own, and it keeps a copy of: Your own notes , everything you post, like, zap and save. Notes that mention you , from people you trust (see Who Can Reach You ). Your direct messages , still encrypted. Recent notes from people you follow , so your feed loads fast. Older ones are cleared out over time. Your media , in its own media server. The vault's address ( wss://127.0.0.1: on a phone) only works on that device. Other apps and people can't connect to it directly. What reaches it over the mesh or the web is set out in Who Can Reach You . Your notes still go to your normal relays too. The vault is the copy you own. To see it explained in the app, open Settings → Help → Tutorials and play Your Vault at Work or How Your Vault Works . iPhone and Android The Vault tab The Vault tab opens on Vault , a list of everything new. Tap the Vault button at the bottom right (or pick Vault Dashboard at the end of the mode menu) to see how your vault is doing. At the top it says Your vault is running , starting, paused or needs a restart, with how long it's been up. If it stops, a button lets you start it again so it catches up on new notes and messages. The menu on that card has Copy Address , Restart , Stop and Start . Below that: Is it safe? : four checks (your key, a saved follow list, a copy on your Mac, a backup file), with a button to make a backup. Who can reach you : how many people can send to your inbox, and how many people you've blocked. In your vault : how many events it holds and how much space notes, media and cache use. The cache is other people's media kept for quick loading, and you can clear it. Keep it full : Import notes , import media, back up media and export notes. Vault settings : shortcuts to Relays, Who Can Reach You, Media Servers, Sync with Vault on Mac and Start automatically. Then relay activity, and Advanced with relay details and media servers. On iPhone and Android this screen is called Vault Dashboard . With more than one account on the device, chips over the Vault list switch between All and each account. Each chip shows that account's new count, and each line is marked with its account. Settings Vault settings Everything about the vault is grouped under Settings → Your Vault . The card at the top of Settings shows whether it's running, with a Start Vault button if it isn't. Start Vault Automatically : start the vault when the app opens. Leave it on. Home vault sync : send your notes and photos to Nostr Vault on your Mac (see The mesh ). Who Can Reach You : who may send to your inbox and messages. More . Import Notes : fill the vault with your past notes. See below. Backup & Restore : save or restore your vault as a file. More . Bring your history Import your past notes A new vault starts empty. Import Notes pulls your old notes, and notes where you are tagged, from your other relays into the vault, starting at a date you pick. Open Settings → Your Vault → Import Notes and set the Start Date . Run it from the Vault Dashboard: Keep it full → Import notes . On Android you can also tap Start Import on the Import Notes page. It reads from the relays that have Import switched on in Settings → Relays . Notes that tag you are kept only if they come from people you trust, or if they reply to or quote your own posts. Where it runs Phone, Mac and web Where the vault runs What's different iPhone Inside the app Vault tab with the full dashboard. Android Inside the app Same as iPhone. Mac Inside the menu bar app A simpler Relay Dashboard. Domain & Port lets you give the vault your own domain so your other devices can reach it, and Startup has Launch at Login . Web In your browser's storage A Vault Dashboard like the phone's, without Start/Stop, Import media or Home vault sync. Import with Keep it full → Import notes or Import from my re

d: Nostr Vault's Who Can Reach You settings: Follow Distance, Minimum Followers and Refresh Trust List decide which people can send to your vault's inbox and messages. Spam control by Web of Trust.
h: What it controls · Follow Distance, Minimum Followers, Refresh Trust List · Who can see what · Phone, Mac and web
x: The basics What it controls Your vault has an inbox, where notes that mention you land, and a chat store for your direct messages. Anyone on Nostr can try to send to them. Who Can Reach You keeps out everyone who isn't close to you in your follows. This is your Web of Trust, and it's the vault's spam filter. Mentions and messages from people outside your trust list are turned away. Replies and quotes of your own posts still get in, from anyone. Your messages can only be read by people on the list who sign in. Your own notes aren't affected. You can always post. Open it from Settings → Your Vault → Who Can Reach You , or tap Who can reach you on the Vault Dashboard (Vault tab → Vault button), which shows how many people can reach your inbox right now. The settings Follow Distance, Minimum Followers, Refresh Trust List Follow Distance How many follows away someone can be and still reach you. Lower is more private. Distance Who can reach you 1 Only you. 2 You and the people you follow. 3 (default) You, the people you follow, and the people they follow, if enough of your follows follow them (see Minimum Followers). The control stops at 3. An older setting of 4 or 5 shows as 3, which is how the relay always ran it. Minimum Followers At distance 3, how many of the people you follow must also follow someone before they can reach you. The default is 3. Raise it to keep out more strangers, lower it to let more friends of friends in. It has no effect at distance 1 or 2. Refresh Trust List How often the vault rebuilds the list from your follows: Every hour , Every 12 hours , Every day (default) or Every week . Someone you just followed can reach you after the next rebuild. At a glance Who can see what There's no setting for who can see your vault. This is what each kind of visitor gets. Your devices Anyone on the mesh Anyone on the web Notes Yes No Yes, your public notes Private notes Yes No No, only you Photos Yes Only photos named in your public notes Yes, your public photos Messages Yes No Only people who sign in and are within your Follow Distance Your devices are the ones in My Devices . Where to find it Phone, Mac and web iPhone and Mac have the same screen. On the Mac it's in the Settings sidebar. Android has the same settings, and restarts the vault for you when you change one. The web has no trust settings. Its trust list is fixed: everyone your follows follow, shown as 2 hops on its Vault Dashboard. Its Who Can Reach You settings row opens the browser vault's mesh panel, where Who can reach this vault is a list of your own vaults' mesh addresses. Not getting a mention you expected? The sender may be too far from you. Follow them, or raise Follow Distance, then wait for the next trust list refresh.

d: How to back up and restore Nostr Vault: export and import notes and media in Backup & Restore, restore an old follow list from Following Backup, un-delete posts in Recently Deleted, and the web backup.
h: Backup & Restore · Following Backup · Recently Deleted · Backups on the web
x: Notes and media Backup & Restore Open Settings → Your Vault → Backup & Restore . It has two parts, and each one is its own file. Notes. Export Notes saves everything in your vault as a .zip: your notes, private notes, messages (still encrypted), the notes that mention you and your feed cache. Import Notes puts a notes backup back. Media. Export Media saves the photos and videos in your vault's media server as a .zip. Import Media puts them back. On iPhone the file goes to the share sheet, so you can save it to Files or send it to your Mac. On the Mac and Android you pick where to save it. A restore adds to what's already in the vault. Anything it already has is skipped, and nothing is deleted. The vault pauses for a moment while notes are saved or restored. Your keys are not in the backup. A backup holds notes and media only. Keep your key (or your signer) safe on its own; see Accounts & Keys in the app. On iPhone and Mac, start the vault before you export media. On iPhone and Android, the Vault tab has the same exports under Keep it full : Export notes and Back up media . Your follow list Following Backup A follow list on Nostr is one list that gets replaced every time it changes. A buggy app can wipe it. Nostr Vault keeps a snapshot each time your list changes, up to 50, on your device. Open Settings → Following Backup . Pick a snapshot. It shows who you no longer follow and who was added since. You can re-follow one person, or tap Restore This List to put the whole list back. Confirm. The restored list replaces your current one and is published to your relays. If your list was wiped somewhere else, Scan Relays looks for older copies of it on your relays. Undo a delete Recently Deleted Posts you delete on a device stay in Settings → Recently Deleted on that device for 30 days. Un-delete posts it again as a new post. Likes and replies on the old post don't come back. Delete Forever removes the copy now. Profiles, lists and articles aren't kept here. Recently Deleted is in the apps and the web app. In the browser Backups on the web The web app keeps its vault in your browser, so back it up if it holds anything you don't have elsewhere. Settings → Backup & Restore : Export notes saves your notes, private notes, messages, the notes that mention you and feed cache as the same .zip the phone apps make, so either one restores the other. Then tap Save backup file to keep it. Photos and videos aren't in it. Vault Dashboard → Keep it full → Back up media saves this browser's photos and videos as a .zip. The web app can't import media. Import notes reads that .zip back. It also reads a .jsonl backup from an older web app. Nothing is published either way. Notes Media Follow snapshots Recently Deleted iPhone .zip .zip Yes Yes Android .zip .zip Yes Yes Mac .zip .zip Yes Yes Web .zip .zip (export only) Yes Yes

d: Media servers (Blossom) in Nostr Vault: where photos go when you post, adding and removing servers, mirroring copies back to your device, the Media & Cache settings, and uploading from the share sheet.
h: What a media server is · Where a photo goes when you post · Add or remove a media server · Mirroring · Deleting a photo · Media & Cache · Uploading from the share sheet · Your device as a photo server
x: The basics What a media server is Relays only carry text. A photo or video is too big for that, so it goes to a media server instead, and your note holds a link to it. Nostr media servers speak a shared language called Blossom , so any Nostr app can read from them. A photo on a Blossom server is named by its fingerprint (a hash of the file). The same photo has the same name on every server, so it can be copied between servers and still be checked. Your account publishes a list of your media servers. Other apps read that list to find your files. When you post Where a photo goes when you post The app first saves the photo on this device, in your vault. It then uploads it to all of your outside media servers at once. As soon as one of them has it, the note is sent. The other servers keep uploading in the background. If no outside server takes the photo, the post is not lost. It waits under Settings → Media Servers in Waiting to send , and sends itself when a server answers. Tap Try sending now to retry straight away, or tap the bin next to a post to drop it. Posting a photo still needs a public media server. A photo that is only on your phone can't be seen by anyone else, so the app won't post it without an outside server. Your list Add or remove a media server Open Settings → Media Servers . It sits in the Relays group, under Relays. Add: type the server's address (for example blossom.example.com ) in the box and tap the add button next to it. If you leave out https:// , the app adds it. Remove: tap the red button next to a server (a minus sign on iPhone and Mac, a bin on Android). Under Suggested , tap Add next to a well-known server to add it. Prices and limits are set by each server. Each change is saved and your updated list is published to your relays. If you set up Home vault sync , your Mac is used as a media server too. It shows at the top of the page and you don't need to add it by hand. In the web app , the same page is Settings → Media Servers . Use Add and Remove , or add one from Suggested. Each saved server is checked when the page opens, and Test checks it again. After a change, tap Save and publish , or Discard changes . The web app uploads to the server marked first first. If you have never published a list, it starts from two default servers. It also needs at least one server in the list. There is no button to reorder servers. In the web app, a server you add goes to the end of the list. Copies you own Mirroring Mirroring brings your own photos back from your media servers into your vault on this device, so they work offline and you keep a copy if a server goes away. Both controls are on the Media Servers page: Mirror Now downloads your media from your outside servers to this device, once. It shows progress while it runs. Auto-Mirror Media keeps doing it for you. Taking a photo down Deleting a photo In Media, hold a photo: Delete from media servers removes it from your outside media servers, any server in your published list and the server in its link. It keeps the copy on this device and on your home vault. Delete everywhere removes those copies too, and offers to delete the posts that use it. The web app has only Delete from media servers. Other people's photos Media & Cache When you look at photos and videos in the feed, the app keeps temporary copies so they load faster next time. You control this in Settings → Media & Cache , in the Feed & Display group. The web app doesn't have this page. Autoplay Videos plays videos as you scroll. Prefetch Profile Pictures loads profile pictures ahead of time for smoother scrolling. Disable Media Cache stops saving copies, so media downloads again each time. Keep Media For sets how long copies are kept: 1, 3, 7, 14 or 30 days, or Never (they don't expire). It starts at 3 days. On iPhone and Mac the oldest copies are still cleared once the cache passes 500 MB. Clear Media Cache deletes the temporary copies to free space. Your vault and your media servers are not touched.

d: How Nostr Vault share links work: Share and Copy Link make a nostrvault.app/thread/ link that opens the post in any browser as a guest, with a link preview card. Plus sharing photos into the app.
h: Share or copy a link · The link preview · Opening a link, with or without an account · Sharing photos into Nostr Vault
x: Sharing a post Share or copy a link Open the menu on any post. Share opens your phone's or browser's share sheet, so you can send the link in a message, an email or another app. Where a browser has no share sheet, it copies the link. On Android it's titled Share Note . Copy Link (Android and web: Copy link ) puts the link on your clipboard and shows Link copied . The link looks like https://nostrvault.app/thread/nevent1 . The nevent part names the post and its author, so the link works without any account and doesn't depend on one relay. Articles, videos and other posts have a Share button too, and give the same kind of link. A live stream's link ends in naddr1 instead. Its menu also has Share as a note , which starts a note saying "Live now: host " with the stream's live card. In a chat or a feed The link preview When you paste the link in a chat app or a social site, it shows a preview card: the author's name (" on Nostr"), the start of the post, and the photo if the post has one. What they see Opening a link, with or without an account The link opens the post in the Nostr Vault web app, in any normal browser. No account? They read the post and its replies as a guest. A bar at the bottom says Viewing as a guest , with Get the app and Sign in . They can open profiles and come back to the post. Hashtags and messages ask them to sign in. Want to reply or like? Liking, replying, reposting and zapping need them to sign in. After signing in, the web app opens on the same post. Already signed in to the web app in that browser? The post opens in their account. A guest visit keeps nothing. Nothing is signed, and nothing is saved in the browser once the tab is closed. Photos load from their usual media server. If one can't be loaded there, the browser fetches it from the author's own device over the mesh. See The mesh . Deleted posts. If the author deletes the post, the link says This post was deleted by its author. Anyone who already saw it may still have a copy, as with anything you post publicly on Nostr. The other direction Sharing photos into Nostr Vault You can also send photos and videos from your Photos app or gallery to Nostr Vault, to upload them to your media server (Blossom). iPhone: pick up to 20 photos and 20 videos, tap Share, choose Nostr Vault, then Add to the upload queue . Open Nostr Vault, or tap the Ready to upload to your media servers notification, to finish the upload. Android: share one or more photos or videos to Nostr Vault. The upload starts right away and shows Uploading to your media servers . Set up your account first. Uploading needs a public media server; see Settings → Media Servers .

d: Share profile in Nostr Vault: a QR code and a nostrvault.app/p/ link for any profile, Copy link and Share, and what happens when someone scans or opens the link.
h: Open the share sheet · Opening a profile link · Who told you about Nostr Vault? · On each device
x: Share profile Open the share sheet Your own profile: tap the QR code button (Android: the share button) next to Edit Profile . Anyone else's profile: open the menu and tap Share profile . The sheet shows a large QR code with the person's name and picture, and three ways to pass it on: Show the code. Someone points a phone camera, or the scanner in Nostr Vault, at it. Copy link puts the link on your clipboard and says Copied . Share opens the system share sheet, so you can send the link in a message, an email or another app. The link looks like https://nostrvault.app/p/npub1 . It carries only the public key, never a secret key. The other side Opening a profile link Scanned or pasted in Nostr Vault. The code from the setup scanner, or a link pasted into Search , opens the profile straight away. Search also takes a bare npub, an nprofile or a nostr: link. Opened in a browser (a tapped link, or a code scanned with the phone camera). The page shows the profile's name, picture and bio, with Open in Nostr Vault to jump into the app, Get Nostr Vault if they don't have it, and Open in another Nostr app . New to Nostr Vault? If they open the link and then install and set up the app, the person who shared it is already filled in on the Who told you about Nostr Vault? step. See below . During setup Who told you about Nostr Vault? A new account starts with an empty feed. One setup step fixes that with the person who brought you here. Tap Scan their profile code , or paste their profile link or npub and continue. Tap Skip, nobody told me to leave the step out. Their profile card shows, so you can check it's them. Tap Follow with their name, or Not them? Try another . Next come up to 10 people they follow, the ones most followed by their other follows first, all ticked. Untick anyone you'd rather not follow. Tap the button that says how many you'll follow. You follow them and everyone still ticked, as one follow list, once setup finishes. When you create an account, the step comes after your profile and the servers step on iPhone, and straight after your profile on Android. When you bring an account you can post with, it comes after the relay check (Android: right after you enter your key). On Android the buttons read Skip and Not them? Change. Read-only accounts skip it. Details for each device: iPhone , Android , Mac . On each device iPhone, iPad and Android have everything on this page. A profile link opened before setup fills in the Who told you step. Mac has Share profile, and a link pasted into Search opens the profile. Links don't open the Mac app from a browser, so paste the link into the Who told you step yourself. Web has Share profile (QR code, Copy link, Share) on every profile.

d: Fixes for common Nostr Vault problems: empty feed, signer not answering, read-only account, photo posts failing, relays not answering, mesh devices not in reach, Check sync stopping, Home vault mode paused.
h: My feed is empty · I can't post, like or follow · My signer never answers · My photo post didn't send · A relay isn't answering · Android: my vault went quiet after an update · A device on My Devices is never in reach · Check sync stops early · Someone's photos don't load over the mesh · Home vault mode paused · Still stuck?
x: My feed is empty You see "No Following Feed". Nostr has no algorithm, so a new account starts with nothing: you see posts from people you follow. Fix: follow a few people. Fill Your Feed helps you find them by topic, and five follows builds your web of trust, which fills Discover and Global too. Replay it from Settings → Help → Tutorials . More on Feeds . Global and Media also stay empty until your web is built. That's on purpose: they show nothing rather than everyone. I can't post, like or follow You see "Read-only for now", "No private key stored for this account" or "This account is read-only. Add its key to follow." You signed in with an npub or a name@domain, which lets you look but not sign. Fix: add the account's key or connect a signer in Settings → Accounts & Keys . My signer never answers You see "Your signer didn't answer in time", "Clave didn't answer" or, on Android, "Amber signing was cancelled or timed out". Your signer app has a request waiting that you haven't approved, or it can't reach its relay. Fix: open the signer app, approve the pending request, then tap Retry in Nostr Vault. If it says "Couldn't reach your signer's relay", check your connection. "This signer is for a different account" means the signer holds another key than the account you picked. My photo post didn't send You see "Your post wasn't sent: no outside media server is set up". A photo has to sit on a public media server so other people can see it, even with the mesh. Fix: add a server in Settings → Relays → Media Servers , then post again. If it says your Mac didn't take the photo, check that Nostr Vault is open on your Mac. "Saved on this device" means the post will send itself as soon as the server answers. A relay isn't answering In the relay list you see " relay isn't answering". It didn't answer just now. Relays go down. Fix: leave it a while. If it stays down, remove it, then tap Save : nothing in the relay list changes until you save. "No Write relay" means none of your relays is set to Write. Your posts still go out, to the default relays the message names, but mark at least one of yours as Write so they go where you choose. Android: my vault went quiet after an update Installing an update stops the app, and with it your vault. Fix: open the app once after updating. Keep Start Vault Automatically on: newer builds then start the relay again by themselves after an update. A device on My Devices is never in reach Under Settings → Mesh → My Devices a device stays "Not in reach" (Android shows when it was last seen). A Mac or a home vault only answers devices that are on its own My Devices list, and a Mac with an empty list doesn't start the mesh at all. Fix: add the devices both ways. On each device, copy the address under This Device and add it on the other one; on your phones, add the Mac as Home vault · full history . Check that Mesh is on, on both. See My Devices . Check sync stops early On iPhone and Android, Check home vault sync ends on "Stopped · N still missing", "Copy didn't finish" with a reason, or "Copy was interrupted". The button is greyed out while a copy is running or when your vault isn't running. Fix: read the reason line. "Copy was interrupted" means the app closed during the copy; it picks up again the next time the relay starts. Anything that couldn't be copied is tried again once a day, and tapping the button starts a new run. Someone's photos don't load over the mesh Your app only asks the mesh for photos from people you follow, and only if they list their own vault as a media server. Files over 32 MB always come from the normal web address. This is about whose photos your app loads. It doesn't change who can see yours. Fix: follow them, and check they have the mesh turned on. Otherwise the photo loads from its web address as usual. Home vault mode paused On iPhone you get "Home vault mode paused". Leaving the app pauses Home vault mode. Fix: tap the notification or open the app again; Home vault mode turns ba

d: Nostr Vault FAQ: which version is current, can I use my existing Nostr account, which relays my posts go to, do I need a Mac, is my home IP public, who can see my photos, losing a phone, what the web app does, is it free.
h: Which version is current? · Is it free? Is it open source? · What is the vault? · Can I use my existing Nostr account? · Which relays do my posts go to? · Do I need a Mac? · Why does posting a photo still need a server? · Is my home IP public? · Who can see my photos over the mesh? · What if I lose my phone? · What can the web app do?
x: Which version is current? 3.0 on iPhone, Mac and Android. It adds the mesh, which connects your own devices directly. These pages describe 3.0. Is it free? Is it open source? Yes to both. The app is free and the code is MIT licensed, on GitHub . What is the vault? Your vault is a personal Nostr relay and a media server, running on your phone. It keeps your notes, your messages and your photos on the device. Nobody on the network can connect to it, unless you share it with your own devices over the mesh. Can I use my existing Nostr account? Yes. Tap I already use Nostr instead of Create an account . iPhone and Mac: paste your nsec, an encrypted key (ncryptsec) or a bunker link, or Use a signer app and Sign in with Clave . Android: paste a key or bunker link, Use Amber , or Use a signer app . Web: Sign in with extension or Connect bunker . The web app never takes the nsec of an account you already have. An npub or name@domain also works, read-only: you can look around but not post. Which relays do my posts go to? The Write relays in Settings → Relays . A new account starts with five, for reading and writing, on iPhone, Mac, Android and the web: relay.primal.net, relay.damus.io, relay.snort.social, relay.btcforplebs.com and nostr-pub.wellorder.net. If your list has no Write relay, posts still go out, to those defaults. Your own vault always keeps a copy. The web app also sends every post to relay.btcforplebs.com, relay.damus.io and relay.snort.social, so a short write list still reaches the wider network. Edits to your relays are kept only when you tap Save (on the web, Save and publish ), which also publishes your relay list for other apps. Do I need a Mac? No. Your phone runs its own vault. A Mac is an optional extra: as Home vault · full history it can hold a full copy and serve your photos while it's on. A spare phone in Home vault mode can do the same job. Why does posting a photo still need a server? Other people need to be able to see it, from any app, whether or not your phone is on. So a photo you post also goes to a public media server. The mesh is an extra, faster place to fetch it from, not a replacement. If posting fails . Is my home IP public? No. Once you add a device, only your own devices learn your phone's address. Anyone else gets your public photos and never your address, but the mesh's middle server does see it. You can change or turn off the middle server under the mesh's Advanced settings. Who can see my photos over the mesh? Your own devices get everything. h: Build Nostr Vault
x: The mesh address is one new entry form, fipsmesh://<npub>/ , in lists you already use: the media server list ( kind:10063 ) and, later, the relay list ( kind:10002 ). In a relay list it goes in its own fipsmesh tag, not an r entry, so clients without mesh support never try to connect to it; Nostr Vault doesn't publish that tag yet. No new event kinds. Requests are plain Blossom GET /<sha256> , with the same hash check. A client that doesn't know the form skips it and carries on with the other servers in the list. A client that does can ask the device for the photo by its fingerprint, the same way it asks any media server, and throws the photo away if the fingerprint doesn't match. Draft, not yet submitted NIP-F1: Nostr over the FIPS Mesh The address form, transport, safety rules for serving and reading, and where Nostr Vault implements each part.
